note: P56 correction artifact: the width-rate story resolved. The original three-point curve (gate_law_width_curve.json) claimed an identical q=0.75 recipe across widths; the machine-written run configs show the d512 run was launched at q=0.8. The seed-43 'attractor hardening' runs (also launched at q=0.8) accidentally completed a 2x4 q-width grid that separates the two variables cleanly.

q_width_grid.source: results/pos_d1024_metrics.jsonl final eval, ARM machine solo

finding_1_rate_is_a_dial: The cumulative 50M gate rate is set by q alone and is width-invariant: five q=0.8 runs across an 8x width range (d128..d1024, two seeds) land inside 0.1981..0.1994 (0.13pp scatter, seed delta at d512 is 0.02pp); the two q=0.75 runs land at 0.2472 twice. The 4.9pp 'fall at d512' in the original curve was the q flip, not width. The original artifact's open question (why the gate fires less at d512) is answered: it does not — that run had a different dial setting.
finding_2_ratio_crossing: At fixed q=0.8 and matched dose (~19.8-19.9%, 9.90-9.97M gradient tokens), the improvement ratio crosses 1.0 at d1024: 0.9708 (d128) -> 0.9892 (d256) -> 0.9777/0.9758 (d512, two seeds agree, the valley is real) -> 1.0092 (d1024). The gated arm ends 0.030 nats BETTER than the full-gradient arm on 19.8% of the gradient tokens. The d128->d256 rise replicates at both q levels (0.9729->0.9953 at q0.75, 0.9708->0.9892 at q0.8).
finding_3_efficiency_corrected: At fixed q=0.8, improvement per million gradient tokens FALLS monotonically with width (0.3696 -> 0.3629 -> 0.3547/0.3467 -> 0.3305). The old 'efficiency grows with width' read (0.2969/0.2937 -> 0.3547) compared q=0.75 doses against a q=0.8 dose: the higher quantile doses fewer, more selective tokens, which raises per-token improvement regardless of width. P56(a)'s registered bar (d1024 >= 0.3547) reads FAIL, and the pre-committed falsifier fires: the per-token efficiency curve has its maximum before d1024. The width-clean statement is the ratio, and the ratio culminates in the d1024 crossing.
still_open: The 24.7% side of the attractor claim (q=0.75, two widths, one seed each) still needs its seed-43 pair AT q=0.75 — relaunched as the completing runs for P56(c).
anchor_caveat: All points share the 50M-token anchor; A2 degrades with width at fixed tokens (4.93 -> 5.04 -> 5.09/5.14 -> 5.45), so the anchor sits earlier in a wider model's training. Absolute improvements (A1-A3) shrink with width for both arms; the ratio normalizes this, per-token efficiency does not.
